business_problem: Tata Chemicals technicians had to navigate extensive maintenance documentation for complex equipment spanning generations of engineering, which slowed fault resolution and made onboarding difficult.
solution_summary: Tata Chemicals deployed Samartha Sarathi, a GenAI advisor for factory technicians, using Microsoft Azure and Azure OpenAI to make maintenance knowledge conversational. The project digitizes manuals, specifications, SOPs and troubleshooting guides into searchable content; technicians use free-text chat or voice-in/voice-out to ask about machine operation, diagnose faults, explore root causes and get recommended fixes. Azure OpenAI responses can include tagged equipment images, and Azure Translation services, fine-tuned for Gujarati, localize guidance for technicians. The implementation began with auto-packer troubleshooting and is extending to drives, generators, filtration-plant automation and instruments. The source does not identify a specific document-ingestion, vector-store, or data-management product, so those lower-level components are not inferred.
